why: I compared the builder brief's examples and test cases with the verifier's probes. They overlap. Builder step 1 gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('7', 3) === '  7'", and step 4 has the builder write tests with padLeft('12345', 5, '0') === '12345' and padLeft('123456', 5, '0') === '123456'. Verifier Check 1 probes p('42',5,'0') expecting "00042" and p('7',3) expecting "  7". Check 2 probes '12345' and '123456' with the same expected outputs. So the builder gets a set of inputs with expected outputs that also appears in the verifier brief. That is a shared probe. The criterion allows telling the builder to write its own tests, but not dictating the checker's exact cases. Builder step 3 also mirrors Check 3: it says to check that every exported function has its own README section. Because the verifier's probes leak into the builder brief, the criterion fails.
